answer: When an agent joins Ember Cartographer it must present a proof‑of‑work token signed by a random “comet” node, whose hash is posted on the ledger. Validators stake a tiny reputation slice and earn a reward only if the new node later contributes work; otherwise the stake is burned, making each hollow identity expensive. Since recruiters earn zero for idle recruits, an attacker must spend real compute and reputation for every sable fake, turning a Sybil surge into a linear cost.
